# 1 Enoch Chapter 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 19 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 19:1 — rendering the angels' deceptive activity

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "having-assumed many-different forms — are defiling mankind" | Preserves Ge'ez participial chain with hyphens |
| LOGOS | "taking on many forms, have been defiling humanity" | Formal; present perfect for ongoing defilement |
| PNEUMA | "taken on countless disguises, corrupting humanity" | "Disguises" adds deceptive nuance; "countless" expands "many" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "taking on many forms, have been defiling humanity." EMET's hyphen chains obscure readability; PNEUMA's "countless disguises" over-interprets. LOGOS balances precision with clarity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:1 — "offering sacrifices to demons as to gods"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "offering-sacrifices to demons as unto gods" | Literal hyphenation; archaic "unto" |
| LOGOS | "sacrifice to demons as to gods" | Formal verbal construction |
| PNEUMA | "worshiping demons as though they were gods" | "Worshiping" broadens beyond sacrifice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "sacrifice to demons as to gods." The Ge'ez specifies cultic sacrifice; PNEUMA's "worshiping" flattens this specificity. EMET's "unto" is unnecessarily archaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:2 — "sirens"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sirens" | Direct retention of Greek loanword in Ge'ez |
| LOGOS | "sirens" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "sirens" | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three agree. "Sirens" retained as the Ge'ez uses a direct Greek loanword (siren < Σειρήν).

**Status:** No disagreement.

---

## 19:3 — Enoch's unique vision claim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no man shall see as I have seen" | Future tense "shall see" |
| LOGOS | "no man has seen what I have seen" | Perfect tense; retrospective claim |
| PNEUMA | "No other human being has witnessed what I have seen" | Expanded phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The perfect tense better captures the retrospective, completed-vision claim. EMET's future is defensible but less natural. PNEUMA is accurate but unnecessarily wordy.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
